notes: Cross-verse split with PRO.9.15. Both verses write a bare Hebrew direct object that the ASV reaches through a supplied English preposition; 9.15 gave that preposition to the verb under rule 44 and 9.9 gave it to the noun under rule 33. לֶקַח is the direct object of the Hiphil יָסַף exactly as אֹרְחוֹתָם is of the Piel יָשַׁר, so rule 44's supplied-preposition clause governs both and rule 33's own third limit defers to it. The *in* (t021) moves from the noun's unit into the verb's; the verb's head stays on the lexical verb, which rule 44 leaves unaffected.
